key_insight: TDFold reframes 3D protein structure prediction as a 2D image-like diffusion problem—diffusing and denoising geometric templates—yielding higher accuracy, faster inference, and lower compute than top competitors.
problem_solved: Accurate and efficient single-sequence protein structure prediction without heavy reliance on MSAs or large template databases; reduces computational cost and improves scalability for one-sequence scenarios.
method: Encode 3D geometry as 2D image-like geometric templates (pairwise distances, orientations, and related maps) conditioned on sequence.
Apply a 2D diffusion/denoising model to iteratively refine geometric templates from noisy to accurate representations.
Decode refined 2D templates back into 3D coordinates via a fast reconstruction module, enabling rapid and accurate structure output.
impact: Offers AI/ML practitioners a scalable, compute-efficient alternative for structure prediction and design workflows—enabling faster inference for single-sequence tasks and easier integration into high-throughput pipelines.

paper_title: Two-dimensional geometric template diffusion for boosting single-sequence protein structure prediction
paper_authors: Xudong Wang, Tong Zhang, Zhen Cui, Xu Guo, Fuyun Wang
